# OTLP egress config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/otlp-egresses/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.OTLPEgressBlock` (ADR-083 D6) declaring an **OTLP push exporter** over a feed: it consumes the selection a `feed` block declares and pushes the selected records to an external collector over OTLP/HTTP. The block label is the egress name. This is the second ADR-083 transport and it is what satisfies ADR-047 Alt C — before it, telemetry terminated on the daemon's internal `_sys/v1/otel-{traces,logs}/v1/...` topics and the only externally reachable signal was the pull-based Prometheus scrape.

**There is no selection here, and its absence is the design.** `subscribe`, `where` and `max_rate_per_sec` are attributes of the referenced feed and are deliberately not restatable on this block — gohcl rejects an attribute the struct does not declare, so an author who tries to narrow at the transport gets a load error rather than a second, divergent filter. A transport references a feed; a feed never references a transport. If an OTLP deployment needs selection behaviour a feed cannot express, that is a change to the `feed` schema (ADR-083 D1), not an attribute added here.

**`principal` is required**, and it is the load-bearing field. ADR-083 D2 authorizes each of the feed's expanded topic filters against the connecting principal's own grants — but a push exporter has no connecting client, so it names the identity it exports *as*. Without one, the only coherent readings would be 'the feed confers reach' (the delegation model D2 rejects, editable in a config file nobody reviews as a security surface) or 'export nothing'. With one, the exporter's reach is a property of that principal's role bindings and changes through an RBAC review. A principal granted none of the feed's filters fails startup loudly rather than running as a silent exporter.

Everything else on the block is genuinely this transport's own concern, because a collector expects to be **pushed to** rather than to dial in: the endpoint and its auth `header` blocks, `compression`, batching (`batch_max_records` / `batch_timeout`), retry (`max_retries` / `retry_initial_backoff` / `retry_max_backoff`) and the depth of the broker queue it drains. The endpoint is a **base** URL — the OTLP/HTTP spec paths `/v1/traces` and `/v1/logs` are appended per signal, so one endpoint serves both and an endpoint that already carries a signal path is rejected rather than double-appended.

## Example

A minimal `otlp-egresses`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/otlp-egresses/example-otlp-egress.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

otlp_egress "example-otlp-egress" {
  feed      = "example-feed"
  principal = "example-principal"
  endpoint  = "https://example.internal"
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | Egress name — the identity this exporter is reported and logged under. |
| `description` | string | no | — | — | — | Human-readable description of what this egress exports and to where. |
| `feed` | string | yes | — | — | — | Name of the feed block this egress consumes. Required. The feed's subscribe list, where predicates and max_rate_per_sec are this egress's only selection — none of them is restatable here (ADR-083 D1). |
| `principal` | string | yes | — | — | — | Principal this egress exports as. Required — ADR-083 D2 authorization is decided against this principal's own grants, so the exporter's reach is a property of its role bindings and not of the feed. A principal granted none of the feed's filters fails startup rather than exporting nothing. |
| `groups` | string[] | no | — | — | — | Groups the export identity carries when its feed is authorized. Optional — omit when roles are bound to the principal directly. |
| `endpoint` | string | yes | — | — | — | Collector OTLP/HTTP base URL (e.g. https://collector:4318). Required. The spec signal paths /v1/traces and /v1/logs are appended, so do not include one. |
| `header` | block (list) | no | — | — | — | Headers sent with every export request — this transport's auth surface. Values are credential references (env:// \| keychain:// \| vault://) or literals. |
| `compression` | string | no | — | — | — | Request body encoding: gzip (default) or none. |
| `batch_max_records` | integer | no | — | — | — | Maximum records coalesced into one export request. Default 100; must be positive when set. |
| `batch_timeout` | string | no | — | — | — | How long a partial batch waits before being flushed anyway (e.g. "5s"). Default 5s. |
| `request_timeout` | string | no | — | — | — | Per-request timeout for one export call (e.g. "30s"). Default 30s. |
| `max_retries` | integer | no | — | — | — | Retries for a retryable export failure before the batch is dropped. Default 4; an explicit 0 disables retry. Drops are counted and logged, never silent. |
| `retry_initial_backoff` | string | no | — | — | — | First retry delay, doubling per attempt (e.g. "1s"). Default 1s. |
| `retry_max_backoff` | string | no | — | — | — | Ceiling on the exponential retry delay (e.g. "30s"). Default 30s. |
| `queue_max_depth` | integer | no | — | — | — | Depth of the broker queue this egress drains. Default 10000. A full queue sheds records and counts them rather than back-pressuring the daemon's telemetry producers. |

## `header` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | Header name (e.g. "Authorization"). |
| `value` | string | yes | — | — | — | Header value: a credential reference (env:// \| keychain:// \| vault://) or a literal. Prefer a reference — a literal is readable by anyone who can read the config. |
